pageCache.text:
Welcome to Stonegate Church of England Primary School
‘Let your light shine’
In our school we believe that every person has special and unique gifts and qualities given to them by God. Through our values of Compassion, Trust, Respect and Courage, we seek to be a school where these gifts are nurtured so that everyone can let their light shine out for all to see.
Let Your Light Shine
Let your good deeds shine out for all to see – Matthew 5:14-16
Welcome to Stonegate Church of England Primary School and Little Acorns Pre-School.
My name is Lucy Hazeldine and it is my privilege to be the Acting Headteacher, working with a wonderful staff team and governors.
We are a small, friendly community that puts Christian Values to its heart and are proud to support all children in a nurturing and safe environment. We have the desire to develop children who achieve highly, are confident and demonstrate the highest attitudes to learning and behaviour. We aim to develop lifelong friends and learners.
As a School Community we are committed to provide the best quality education for all pupils. We are determined to continue to raise standards and support learning through a wide variety of interactive and stimulating environments.
The children of Stonegate are confident to share their successes with others and this is celebrated throughout school life; they are excellent ambassadors for our school.
We provide a wide variety of extra curricular activities and encourage all children to pursue interests and develop their talents in many areas in order to enhance their learning and encourage creativity and success in all they do.
Stonegate Church of England Primary School is a small, rural, Church of England Voluntary Controlled school for boys and girls aged 2 to 11.
The school, established in the mid-nineteenth century, is situated in the village of Stonegate in the heart of the beautiful High Weald of Sussex.
We have capacity for 110 children at the school, coming from the village and the surrounding area.
As well as fulfilling our legal obligation to deliver the National Curriculum to our children, we offer a wide range of enriching activities to develop the whole child and enable each one of our pupils to fulfil their unique potential.
In September 2020, we opened an on site Pre-School to further support our community. Little Acorns is open during term time between 8.45am and 3.15pm.
Our pupils, parents, staff and governors were asked to identify the most important Christian values in school. They chose the following: Friendship, Compassion, Resilience, Respect, Trust and Courage. Children are rewarded for showing any of these qualities around school.
From September 2025 the school went into partnership with Pioneer Federation and hope to federate with them by July 2026. The Pioneer Federation consists of 8 Primary Schools. (East Hoathly Church of England Primary School, Chiddingly Primary School, St Mary the Virgin Church of England Primary School, Park Mead Primary School, Nutley Church of England Primary School,Groombridge St. Thomas Church of England Primary School and Framfield Church of England Primary School).

pageCache.pageTitle: Admissions – Stonegate Church of England Primary School
pageCache.text:
Admissions
Applying for a place at Stonegate CE Primary School
Please contact the School Office if you would like to visit the school or for any further information about in-year admissions, or new starters in 2025-2026.
The closing date to apply for September 2026 school places is 15th January 2026.
We are holding Open Mornings for Parents and Children due to start school in September 2025 on Thursday 9th October, Thursday 13th November and Monday 1st December 2025. Starting at 9.30am, there will be a presentation in the school hall, followed by a tour of the school led by the children of Year 6. Please note no booking is required for our Open Mornings.
Further information for new starters in September 2026
The arrangements for the admission of children to our school at age 4+ are made by East Sussex County Council. A detailed description of the arrangements is contained in the booklet ‘Admission to Primary Schools’
The admissions criteria for community and voluntary controlled schools are as follows:
Priority 1. Looked after children.
Priority 2. Children with an exceptional medical or social need for whom attendance at any other school would be inappropriate.
Priority 3. Children who will have a brother or sister at the school (or a linked infant or junior school) at the time of admission.
Priority 4. Children wishing to transfer between a linked infant and junior school.
Priority 5. Children living within a pre-defined community area.
Priority 6. Children living outside the pre-defined community area.
Tie breaker
If there are more children who qualify under an oversubscription criterion than places available, place allocation will be determined by prioritising applications within that criterion, on the basis of the shortest route from home to school using surfaced, passable route.
For further information and online applications please visit:
www.eastsussex.gov.uk/educationandlearning/schools/admissions

pageCache.pageTitle: Key Information About Our Curriculum – Stonegate Church of England Primary School
pageCache.text:
Key Information About Our Curriculum
Pioneer Vision
Pioneer Vision
‘Being the best that we can be in thriving communities and achieving fullness of life’
We pursue excellence in our classrooms, inclusion in our culture, collaboration across our communities and integrity in all we do – building great Pioneer schools where every child flourishes, every staff member thrives and everyone belongs.
Pioneer Values
Excellence – Inclusion – Collaboration- Integrity
Pioneer Ethos
‘Achievement for All, Learning Together, Learning for Life’
The Pioneer Curriculum
The collaborative Pioneer Curriculum is ambitious, challenging and creative, carefully sequencing knowledge so that children are supported in building a deep understanding across all subject areas. We believe in the importance of providing a high-quality experience that also builds health and well-being individually and collectively. The Pioneer Federation aims to inspire our children to engage confidently with the world and develop the knowledge and skills from across the curriculum that enables them to thrive.
Organisation
Developed collaboratively across the Pioneer Federation, our ambitious, broad and balanced curriculum is carefully sequenced to ensure pupils progressively build, deepen and apply their knowledge and skills over time. Designed specifically for mixed-age classes across Key Stages 1 and 2, our two-year curriculum provides a coherent and systematic pathway that enables all pupils to achieve the National Curriculum expectations and more.
Our Curriculum Overviews set out the strategic intent and sequence of learning across every subject over the two-year cycle. They ensure clear progression and full coverage of the National Curriculum.
Our Subject Overviews explain the intent of each subject, showing how National Curriculum objectives are mapped through carefully sequenced units of learning. They also include our progression of Core and Aspirational Vocabulary, ensuring pupils develop the language needed to become confident learners within each subject.
Our Medium-Term Plans (MTPs) provide the framework for delivering the curriculum each term. They break learning into sequential lesson blocks, identifying the key knowledge, skills, learning activities, expected outcomes and vocabulary for every unit. Each MTP also demonstrates how each school’s unique cultural context is woven into the curriculum. These documents support teachers in planning, adapting and delivering high-quality lessons while ensuring full curriculum coverage.
Our Curriculum & Subject Policies outline the intent, implementation and impact of each curriculum area, demonstrating how our curriculum vision is translated into classroom practice.
Mixed-Age Classes and Curriculum Design
The Pioneer Federation curriculum has been designed specifically for mixed-age classes through a two-year rolling programme. Rather than separating learning by individual year groups, our curriculum provides a shared sequence of progressively-challenging knowledge and skills across each two-year cycle.
Every National Curriculum objective is explicitly mapped within our Medium-Term Plans to ensure that all pupils experience the full curriculum for their year groups over the two years.
Teachers use these documents to deliver lessons with high-quality teaching for all, and adaptations and scaffolds to support children so that the lessons respond to the needs of each cohort. Learning is planned using a ‘stage, not age’ approach, enabling pupils of different ages and abilities to access the curriculum at an appropriate level, while being suitably challenged. This approach ensures every child is supported to make strong progress from their individual starting point.
Adaptation and Inclusion
Our curriculum is designed to be ambitious and accessible for every child.
Teachers adapt planning, teaching and assessment to meet the needs of their individual classes, using the Medium-Term Plans and use ‘Cohort Planning meetings’ to personalise learning for each school and cohort.
At the beginning of every unit, teachers identify pupils’ prior knowledge and build upon it throughout the sequence of learning. This enables teaching to respond directly to pupils’ existing understanding and misconceptions.
Learning is adapted through carefully considered use of language, resources, learning environments, recording methods and assessment approaches, ensuring that every child, regardless of ability, background or starting point, is supported to achieve success and make sustained progress.
Assessment and Monitoring
Assessment is an integral part of teaching and learning and assessments are used to ensure the next steps for learning are clearly defined.
Each unit begins with a Subject Knowledge Organiser, introducing the key vocabulary and essential knowledge pupils will learn. Teachers establish pupils’ prior understanding at the start of each unit before assessing learning throughout the sequence of lessons.
Every unit concludes with a Subject End Point Assessment, enabling teachers to evaluate pupils’ understanding of the key knowledge and skills. These assessments also encourage pupils to reflect on the unit’s overarching enquiry question, promoting deeper thinking and knowledge recall.
Assessment information is used to adapt future planning, address misconceptions and ensure pupils continue to make strong progress. During termly Pioneer Cohort Planning meetings, teachers evaluate the effectiveness of previous Medium-Term Plans before refining subsequent units to meet pupils’ needs.
Subject Leaders from across the Federation regularly monitor the quality of education through subject deep dives, lesson observations, planning reviews and scrutiny of pupils’ work. Senior leaders triangulate this evidence to evaluate teaching, learning and curriculum implementation across the Federation.
Teacher assessments are quality assured through internal moderation, federation-wide cohort moderation, external moderation, pupil tests and regular standardisation training.
Pupil progress is tracked using Pioneer ARBOR tracking and datawalls for all subjects. Termly pupil progress meetings enable teachers and leaders to review attainment, identify pupils requiring additional support and review and plan appropriate interventions.
The Governing Board plays a strategic role in ensuring every school delivers a broad, balanced and ambitious curriculum. Governors monitor curriculum development, pupil outcomes and statutory compliance through regular reports, school visits and analysis of achievement data, providing both support and challenge to school leaders.
Curriculum Sequencing​
The sequence of learning across our curriculum has been carefully planned to maximise progression, engagement and meaningful learning opportunities.
Curriculum sequencing takes account of:
Enrichment
We believe that enrichment is an essential part of a high-quality education. Meaningful experiences beyond the classroom broaden horizons, raise aspirations, deepen learning and contribute significantly to pupils’ personal development.
Through a rich programme of visits, visitors and practical experiences, pupils develop confidence, resilience, teamwork, communication and problem-solving skills while embedding their curriculum learning in meaningful contexts.

pageCache.pageTitle: SEND – Stonegate Church of England Primary School
pageCache.text:
SEND
Sometimes children require additional support and we provide for this through our Inclusion department which is coordinated by our Senco Mrs Leahy(senco@stonegate.e-sussex.sch.uk).
Mrs Phoebe Cameron and Mrs Jessica Tabbah are our SEN Governors.
The school aims to give all children, whatever their ability, equal access to a broad and balanced education. Many children will, at some time in their school career, have special educational needs, requiring support over and above that normally offered in the classroom. The special needs coordinator is responsible, in consultation with class teachers, for identifying children with special needs and the subsequent provision of appropriate help. This will initially be provided within class or small group work. If necessary, help and advice will be sought from outside agencies. Very occasionally a statutory assessment will be made, leading to an Education, Health and Care Plan. All interventions are fully discussed with parents.
We have a dedicated team and facilities to address the needs of all our children and to help them overcome barriers to learning. We are able to provide 1:1 tuition , small group work, or nuture room activities so that every member of our school can achieve at, or above their potential.
Children who are identified as being particularly able, either academically or in the creative arts, are given extension and enrichment opportunities within the classroom, in order to make sure they fulfill their potential. They may also have opportunities to take part in special projects or in after-school clubs.
The Local Offer is what’s available for children and young adults with special educational needs and disabilities up to the age of 25, and their families. This is provide by the Local Authority, further information can be found at:
https://www.eastsussex.gov.uk/childrenandfamilies/specialneeds/localoffer/about/
For a prospectus of services please use the link:
https://czone.eastsussex.gov.uk/inclusion-and-send/send-prospectus/
Dyslexia Friendly Status
As part of our continuing development we have gained Dyslexia Friendly Status. Strategies which help dyslexic pupils learn effectively are often helpful in improving the learning of all pupils.
The admission arrangements for disabled pupils are the same as for any other pupils. In order to provide the most appropriate environment and resources, early notification and discussion with the school and local authority is essential.
Equally pupils who show a particular ability are encouraged to extend their work both in class and through enrichment activities, sometimes with pupils from other schools in the local Cluster.
If you would like anymore information on areas of Special Educational Needs please contact Mrs Leahy at : senco@pioneerfederation.co.uk

Sports Premium
The aims of the National Curriculum for Physical Education ensure that all pupils:
Funding for Primary School PE and Sports
The government is committed to ensuring that children and young people have access to at least 60 minutes of sport and physical activity per day. It recommends 30 minutes of this is delivered during the school day (in line with the Chief Medical Officers guidelines which recommend an average of at least 60 minutes per day across the week).
The PE and sport premium is intended to help primary schools to achieve this commitment, providing primary schools with £320 million of government funding to make additional and sustainable improvements to the quality of the PE, physical activity and sport. The funding has been allocated to primary school head teachers and has been ‘ring fenced’. This means it can only be spent specifically on PE and sport in schools.
All pupils should leave primary school physically literate and with the knowledge, skills and motivation necessary to equip them for a healthy lifestyle and lifelong participation in physical activity and sport.

pageCache.pageTitle: Attendance – Stonegate Church of England Primary School
pageCache.text:
Attendance
We believe that a good attendance habit gives your child the best possible start in life and helps develop the skills needed in adult life.
Start of the day
It is very important to develop good routines for getting to school on time. The parking around the school is very limited, so if you have to travel by car you should allow for this. The school gates are open from 8.30am and children head straight into their classroom ready for registration 8.45am.
Sickness
If your child is unwell, please phone the school before 9.30am and leave a message; if you don’t do this, the school will contact you to find out where your child is.
If your child becomes unwell during the day, we will contact you to come and collect them. Please ensure that we always have up to date telephone numbers for you.
Reducing infections
In terms of length of time needed to recover from a particular illness we follow the Health protection in schools and other childcare facilities produced by Public Health England:
https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/health-protection-in-schools-and-other-childcare-facilities
This gives the recommended times to ensure that childhood illnesses are not spread throughout a school, e.g. for diarrhoea and vomiting it is recommended that a child remains off school for 48 hours from the last bout of illness.
End of the day
The school day for all pupils finishes at 3.15pm. The children are walked by their teacher to the front of the school at the end of the day. Please ensure you collect your child on time.
Holiday during term time
There is no entitlement for parents to remove their child from school for the purpose of holiday in term time. The head teacher will look at each case individually and only authorise holiday in extreme exceptional circumstances. The Local Authority will issue parents with a Penalty Notice of £60 per parent per child for taking holiday during term time. If you do need to take your child out of school other than for medical reasons, please complete a holiday application form which is available from the School Office.

pageCache.pageTitle: PTA – Stonegate Church of England Primary School
pageCache.text:
PTA
What are we?
The Parents Teachers Association (PTA) is just that – a committee of staff and parents working together for the good of the school. The PTA is a bridge between the school and parents and draws them together in a common goal – making Stonegate School the best it can be.
The majority of the PTA’s work focuses on fundraising but linked into this is a social aspect – with family fun days or quiz/race nights, fetes and fairs. The children and parents and teachers are given a way to enjoy the social aspects of school life and also feel part of the wider community of Stonegate village.
The PTA has a core committee – a team of dedicated organisers who set all the wheels in motion for the main fundraising events and extra-curricular activities provided by the PTA. The Committee meet on a regular basis (once a term) – anyone is able to join and new members are always welcome.
What do we do?
Most of the events we run are for fund-raising purposes and most of our funds are raised through the events we run! Throughout the year we have other events or activities – a fantastic quiz night to name but one, but if there are any budding fundraisers out there, bursting with fresh ideas, we’d love to hear them! The PTA are always delighted with any parental help they can get, so even if you’re only able to man a stall for half an hour, your efforts will still be very much appreciated.

Jewellery
The wearing of any jewellery is not allowed. However, if your child has pierced ears then they must wear plain stud earrings. Other earrings will not be permitted. This request applies to both boys and girls. Owing to a number of accidents in schools, East Sussex County Council’s policy is that studs must be removed during all physical education and swimming instruction. The child is responsible for ensuring that this takes place. If your child is unable to remove/replace their own studs they should not be worn to school on P.E. or swimming days. Your child will be unable to participate in the lesson with studs in place. Under no circumstances are staff permitted to remove/replace studs.
Every year a small number of children have their ears pierced during term-time. Parents should be aware that if the studs cannot be removed at all during those first weeks, the child will be unable to participate in PE or swimming.
Accidents can also occur during breaks and lunch times. The school therefore strongly recommends that children should avoid wearing studs in school wherever possible. The school would not wish to make this a major issue but the Staff and Governors would appreciate sensible support from home.

Safeguarding – Stonegate Church of England Primary School
pageCache.text:
Safeguarding
Little Acorns Pre-School shares the systems and process for Safeguarding with Stonegate Primary School.
We at Stonegate Primary School and Little Acorns Pre-School take our Safeguarding responsibilities very seriously. This means that we ensure that everyone working in our school has successfully completed the necessary clearances to enable them to work with children.
It also means that we have staff members who are specifically trained and nominated as the Designated Safeguarding Leads (DSLs) within school. The safeguarding lead is Mrs Lucy Hazeldine and the Deputy DSLs are Mrs Jackson and Miss Heard.
We are all expected to share any concerns we have about staff conduct around children with the Head of School. As in all schools, if there are concerns about the conduct of the Head, then these should be shared with the Chair of Governors (Kevin Millington). The staff ‘Whistleblowing Policy’ has been discussed and adopted and all staff have access to this document.
We also follow the East Sussex Child Protection Procedures and the Local Safeguarding Children’s Board local guidance and have systems in place to share concerns regarding children’s welfare with our DSLs, with parents and with relevant external agencies. Part of our legal duty to safeguard our children, may also include us needing to consult specifically with and take advice from, the Police or Children’s Social Care, should the need arise.
By working closely together as a staff and with our partner agencies, we firmly believe that we will continue to offer a safe learning environment for all our children.
Please take the time to read our policies and do not hesitate to contact the school should you have any questions about the very serious issue.
The direct email for the DSL is: head@stonegate.e-sussex.sch.uk

pageCache.pageTitle: Welcome – Stonegate Church of England Primary School
pageCache.text:
Welcome
Little Acorns Pre-School – ‘From little acorns mighty oaks grow’
On behalf of Little Acorns, I would like to warmly welcome you to our happy and friendly Pre-School.
Starting Pre-School is often a young child’s first steps away from their family environment and we are very aware of the responsibility of this task.
We pride ourselves on fostering an atmosphere of care and security, which is so important in giving children the confidence to try for themselves.
We have fantastic facilities which enable us to provide your child with a varied, fun, educational start to their school lives.
As we are part of the school the children will join the rest of the school for some assemblies, enrichment events and to share learning activities.
They also have a shared play area with the reception children which will help them to become familiar with being in amongst the older ones.
What We Offer
As a Pre-School we have 12 available places for each session of the day (our sessions run between 8.45 to 11.45 and 12.15 to 3.15 each day of the term (lunch is available between 11.45 and 12.15).
With these small numbers of children and our high child to adult ratio we are able to provide rich and exciting development opportunities for every child.
Each day a range of activities are set out in every session which encourage and stimulate learning across the 7 areas of learning. Our team use a number of strategies to ensure that every child leaves these activities with the best experience possible.
We record these interactions using Tapestry. Observations are made regularly on Tapestry and these are sent to parents so they can support their child at home.
Our Additional Provision
We aim to give every one of our ‘Little Acorns’ the widest range of experiences.
Every day there are planned activities which focus on the 7 areas of learning both inside and outside of the classroom. These activities will link to the ‘theme of the week’ or the larger whole term’s learning journey.
Mrs Cassé takes us to Forest School once a week. In addition to this, we are taught PE using a multiskills programme.
Forest School
Forest School – which started in Scandinavia – is all about enabling children to explore and experience the natural world through hands-on activities outdoors. The concept has proven to develop the self-esteem and confidence of pre-school children through activities that involve creativity, working together and child-led learning.
As children explore the natural habitat, they become more in harmony with nature, bringing a sense of belonging and contentment. Forest School is also a place to assess risk in a safe environment. This challenging play helps develop self-confidence, competence, emotional resilience and a sense of independence. Without risk and challenge, children are at risk of losing their sense of aspiration and ambition.
PE
One of the greatest benefits of physical education is to improve the physical health and mental health at the same time. Children who are involved in regular physical education are much more likely to have better physical health when compared to those who don’t. For those children introduced to physical activity of increasing intensity, their hearts and bones are offered a range of benefits.
There is an increase of cases of cardiovascular health issues among children nowadays, so to curb this, the NHS recommends at least an hour of moderate to vigorous physical activity every day for children. There is scientific proof that physical activity minimises obesity in children. This can all be achieved through physical education with the right primary sports equipment. Running and cycling style activities are very useful.
Considering mental health, physical education has the potential to greatly boost children’s memories, as well as improving their concentration. Children are always learning, even at those early years, so having physical education is very important to facilitate their learning. Such opportunities can increase the chance of academic benefits. In many cases, these children can solve a range of complex skills thanks to their improved creativity.

pageCache.pageTitle: EYFS Curriculum – Stonegate Church of England Primary School
pageCache.text:
EYFS Curriculum
Organisation
Our exciting, broad and balanced curriculum is taught across our Nursery and Reception Classes. Each term has a focussed topic theme, and key questions for children to consider.
Key Documents
We use key documents to support the ongoing and reflective development of our curriculum, assessment and planning cycles within the EYFS.
Content and Sequence
The EYFS team across the Federation have reviewed the new framework and supporting documents to plan opportunities that deepen children’s understanding, knowledge, skills and language through linking with their local area and community, and enjoying key texts and topic-themed experiences.
Examples of this include:
The curriculum is sequenced in this order to allow pupils to learn and then embed the core foundations they will need to then build upon in each topic and term. For example, the sequence of systematic approach of teaching phonics and number development in Term 1 and 2 will then enable children to access wider activities and provision in subsequent terms, i.e. recognising amounts will support understanding of addition, and grouping or knowing individual phonic sounds will enable children to start early writing through labelling and letter formation.
Vocabulary, language and communication are key areas that thread throughout our curriculum and experiences giving pupils a variety of opportunities to expand and develop their language skills. In addition pupil’s holistic wellbeing will be supported throughout their early years journey, which will include topics such as oral health, mindfulness and self-regulation.
Our specific areas of learning, (Literacy, Maths, Understanding the World and Expressive Art & Design) have all been planned to support children’s learning in line with their open-ended interests and individual schools’ local areas. Some of the others factors also include:
Impact and Knowledge-gained
The skills and knowledge from the different areas of learning are carefully aligned to ensure a correlated cross-curricular approach to the children’s learning, whilst providing flexibility to adapt and follow the individual cohort interests. The curriculum has been designed to allow children regular opportunities to revisit and embed core-learning skills, such as developing vocabulary & language through playing; exploring, reading, writing and mastering early maths concepts. The timetable of the days (weeks, terms and year) is a careful balance of child initiated learning, play and exploration and regular guided teaching moments.
In Early Years the learning is tailored to individual needs and will be made accessible to children through strategies that work for them, this may include sensory activities, calm or quiet zones, through images or signs, brining learning through a specific interest. Children across our early years environments are supported to feel they can express themselves and staff work closely with the SENCO to develop individualised tasks and curriculums for children that are appropriate.
The curriculum for the Nursery and Reception classes consists of two cycles, with the core intent remaining the same across both. For example, in Term 3, Cycle 1, the topic is entitled ‘Off We Go’ and we focus on transport, as well as on the big question ‘who helps us.’ To support this, we draw on a range of texts, learning experiences and visits. In Term 3, Cycle 2, the topic is entitled ‘Blast Off’ and the prior learning is built on, revisiting some texts and experiences but drawing from many others, with the big question also remaining the same but the range of experiences and texts also being varied and extended.
This is to ensure that the children who begin their education with us in our preschool settings are able to deepen and broaden their knowledge, understanding and experiences over their two year EYFS journey.

Collective Worship – Stonegate Church of England Primary School
pageCache.text:
Collective Worship
Worship at Stonegate Primary School takes place at school and in Church and is led by teachers, members of our community or our Vicar. Children are encouraged to take an active part in every Worship.
Collective worship is planned at the start of each Term by the Headteacher who uses resources and ideas from www.assemblies.org.uk
Children are regularly asked to evaluate Worship to ensure that they feel that the best experiences are being had.
As a Church school all our acts of collective worship are Christian and relate to topics associated with our four Core Values.
All children develop:
Positive attitudes in relation to:
self awareness
respect for all
open-mindedness
appreciation and wonder
general aspects of the PSHE Curriculum
